assets.description:
The player's desk at the start of the game: the open-air workspace of a village sarpanch candidate in a fictional village in rural Bihar, north India. Seen from directly above: a flat top-down view with no perspective distortion.
Composition (16:9): a woven rope charpai with a wooden frame fills the middle two-thirds of the frame and serves as the desk. The centre of the charpai is left clear and uncluttered, because the game places a sheet of paper there. Along the top edge, the base of a thick neem tree trunk with gnarled roots; a tear-off wall calendar with blank pages hangs on a nail in the trunk. The ground around the charpai is packed earth with a few fallen neem leaves.
Objects, each clearly separated with space around it so it can be cut out later:
- left side: an old cream rotary landline phone with a coiled cord; a dented tin cash box
- on the charpai, near its edges: a red cloth-bound bahi-khata ledger; a folded newspaper whose columns are suggested by grey blocks with no readable letters; a small stack of paper files tied with cotton string; a small spiral notebook with a pencil
- right side: a glass of milky chai on a small steel saucer
- bottom-right corner: the front wheel and handlebars of an old black bicycle entering the frame
Dappled neem-leaf shadows fall across the scene.

An old cream-coloured rotary landline telephone with a coiled cord, slightly worn and scuffed, seen from directly above to match the desk scene.

The player's personal assistant: a fictional young man in his mid-twenties from a small north Indian village. Sharp, loyal and a little anxious. Neatly combed hair, thin moustache, simple checked half-sleeve shirt with a pen clipped in the pocket.
One villager standing in a rally crowd, seen from behind and slightly above, head and shoulders and upper body. Simple flat shapes suitable for a crowd silhouette; ordinary everyday clothes.
